diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
The runner instance's user-data script writes the registration token into the SSM parameter `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token`, whose value is otherwise left unmanaged (`ignore_changes = ["value"]`). `aws_ssm_parameter` creates with `overwrite = false`, so the parameter must exist before the instance launches; otherwise the user-data `put-parameter` creates it first and Terraform's create fails with "already exists". `aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance` only receives the parameter's name as a plain string (via `local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key`), so no dependency is inferred and the group may launch instances first. It should depend on `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance` launches the runner EC2 instance whose user-data script writes the registration token into `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` (Terraform creates it with value "null" and ignores later value changes). Nothing orders the ASG after the SSM parameter — the parameter name is only referenced as a string in the template — so the instance may boot and write/create the parameter before Terraform creates it, causing the `aws_ssm_parameter` create to fail (overwrite defaults to false on create). Add `depends_on = [aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token]` to the autoscaling group.
